public_observations.topic: AI CFD Scientist clean-control false positives as requirement-evidence packaging failures
public_observations.observation: The pre-submission ablation implementation makes the four clean-control false positives mechanistically more specific than the paper-level description alone. In interpret mode, scripts/viz.py requests only a residual-trend plot and velocity-magnitude contour. scripts/quick_interpret.py then sends only PNG files from the figures directory plus the full requirement text to the vision LLM; it does not read figures.json, case files, solver dictionaries, logs, or requirement-specific post-processing artifacts. Yet the four clean requirements demand specialized evidence: jet requires probe time-series and dominant lateral-velocity frequency; backward-facing step requires lower-wall Cf and reattachment x; hill requires Cf(x/H), DNS comparison, and Cf RMSE; channel requires a fully developed velocity profile, centerline U, and wall shear stress. Therefore the reported clean false positives are consistent with an evidence-package coverage mismatch: the verifier was asked to judge deliverables that the generic interpret-mode package did not guarantee were visible.
public_observations.boundary: This maps a plausible failure mechanism from public code and the paper's false-positive description; per-case executed decision artifacts are not available on the current GitHub surface to certify each individual run.

public_observations.topic: AI CFD Scientist public run-artifact discoverability boundary
public_observations.observation: The current public GitHub repository ignores runs/ and data/, exposes no runs/nips_2026/vlm_ablation directory at current main, and the GitHub releases collection is empty. Thus the paper-level ablation table and mechanism code are inspectable, but the current GitHub/release surface does not provide a discoverable per-case decision/figure archive that binds the reported verdicts to an exact commit/model/prompt/artifact manifest.
public_observations.boundary: Absence is scoped to the current public GitHub tree and GitHub releases; it does not establish that no artifact was ever distributed elsewhere.

public_observations.observation: Memory Transfer Learning evaluates six coding benchmarks and reports that unified cross-domain memory improves average performance by 3.7%, while low-level traces can induce negative transfer from excessive specificity and abstract insights transfer more reliably. This supports the design concern that transferred memory requires target compatibility, but it is a coding-agent study and does not isolate a receiver-side applicability/revalidation gate with stored memory and retrieval held fixed.
public_observations.boundary: cross-domain coding-agent evidence only; not a matched science-domain revalidation intervention

public_observations.topic: EvoScientist paper-era evo-memory mechanism correspondence and extension boundary
public_observations.observation: The latest direct pre-submission path-touching commit found for EvoSkills/skills/evo-memory is 39a4b20682ecd3adb628704834867915fc320269 from 2026-03-06, three days before EvoScientist v1 submission. At that revision, evo-memory already documents paper-aligned IVE triggers (no executable code within budget or worse-than-baseline result), top-k cosine-style retrieval, and failed-direction memory. Its memory schema additionally stores Evidence, Root Cause, Boundary Conditions, Countermeasures, Do-Not-Repeat Notes, and Retrieval Tags. Crucially, its own paper-prompts.md explicitly says the paper IVE has FAILED/NOT_FAILED with two failure subtypes and that the five-question implementation-vs-fundamental diagnostic is a practical skill extension, not part of the paper prompt. Therefore the historical skill is useful near-submission implementation lineage, but extended failure classification/boundary-handling fields must not be credited to the evaluated paper mechanism without a run-to-skill revision binding.
public_observations.boundary: near-submission official skill lineage is not an explicit evaluated-run dependency pin; skill extensions are separated from paper prompt behavior

protocol_inferences.name: REQUIREMENT_ARTIFACT_COVERAGE_v3
protocol_inferences.rule: Verifier observability must be computed over requirement×artifact membership, not inferred from the existence of some figures. Every declared claim requirement must enumerate a non-empty required artifact set; complete coverage requires every member to be verifier-visible. Hard-negative evidence must reference an artifact that belongs to the cited requirement and match its exact visible digest. Requirement-artifact manifest membership is itself authorization state: membership-digest drift invalidates cached verification.

protocol_inferences.name: evaluated_mechanism_vs_skill_extension
protocol_inferences.rule: When a paper-era support skill explicitly distinguishes paper prompts from practical extensions, evidence handoff must tag each field/rule as paper-core, implementation-extension, or unresolved, and must not transfer causal credit from the extension to the evaluated paper result without an explicit evaluated-revision binding.
